# MusicRaT Development Instructions

## Purpose

MusicRaT is a C++20 real-time audio framework built on CommRaT. Audio sources, processors, sinks, hardware adapters, and control adapters are independently launchable CommRaT modules connected through typed messages.

Use [ROADMAP.md](../ROADMAP.md) for planned work, [docs/AUDIO_CORE.md](../docs/AUDIO_CORE.md) for the current audio block, [docs/SIGNALS_AND_PORTS.md](../docs/SIGNALS_AND_PORTS.md) as the normative routing architecture, and [docs/PROJECT_LAYOUT.md](../docs/PROJECT_LAYOUT.md) for file placement and dependency rules.
Use [docs/EVL_AND_RATOS.md](../docs/EVL_AND_RATOS.md) for EVL portability, RaTOS packaging boundaries, and layered real-time validation.

## Current Architecture

- Public headers live under `include/musicrat/` and use installed-style includes such as `<musicrat/protocol/audio_block.hpp>`.
- `include/musicrat/musicrat.hpp` owns the `MusicRaT` application registry; protocol definitions live under `include/musicrat/protocol/`.
- CommRaT-independent kernels live under `include/musicrat/dsp/`; module adapters live under `include/musicrat/modules/`.
- Minimal `COMMRAT_MODULE_MAIN` wrappers live under `src/modules/`; process-level executables live under `src/apps/`; platform integrations live under `src/backends/`.
- Tests mirror ownership under `tests/protocol`, `tests/dsp`, `tests/modules`, and `tests/integration`.
- `AudioBlock` is a bounded planar block using the CMake-selected sample type.
- Compile-time policy is generated by CMake in `musicrat/config.hpp`; do not hard-code sample type, capacities, default sample rate, or default period in modules.
- Audio policy includes `MUSICRAT_SAMPLE_TYPE`, `MUSICRAT_MAX_AUDIO_CHANNELS`, `MUSICRAT_MAX_AUDIO_FRAMES`, `MUSICRAT_MAX_PARAMETER_EVENTS`, `MUSICRAT_MAX_CONTROL_EVENTS`, `MUSICRAT_MAX_NOTE_EVENTS`, `MUSICRAT_FILE_PROXY_BYTES`, `MUSICRAT_DEFAULT_SAMPLE_RATE_HZ`, and `MUSICRAT_DEFAULT_BLOCK_PERIOD_MS`.
- Active sample rate, channel count, frame count, timestamp, sequence number, and flags are runtime block metadata.
- Modules use `MusicRaT::Module2`, never the removed legacy `Module` API.
- Persistent settings use `commrat::Params<T>`.
- Imperative request/reply actions use commands associated with an output through `commrat::DataWithCommands`.
- Streaming audio and control events use typed `Output<T>` and `Input<T>` connections.
- Command-only dependencies use `commrat::Remote<T>`.
- The pre-launch Application Designer lives under `tools/application-designer`; RatGUI is for runtime operation and LVGL is for on-device controls.

## Module Pattern

```cpp
struct ProcessorParams {
    musicrat::config::sample_type gain{1.0};
};

class Processor : public MusicRaT::Module2<
    commrat::Output<CommRaT::Messages::AudioBlock>,
    commrat::Input<CommRaT::Messages::AudioBlock>,
    commrat::Params<ProcessorParams>
> {
    using Base = MusicRaT::Module2<
        commrat::Output<CommRaT::Messages::AudioBlock>,
        commrat::Input<CommRaT::Messages::AudioBlock>,
        commrat::Params<ProcessorParams>>;

public:
    explicit Processor(const commrat::ModuleConfig& config) : Base(config) {}

protected:
    void process(const CommRaT::Messages::AudioBlock& input,
                 CommRaT::Messages::AudioBlock& output) override {
        // Validate metadata, then process without allocation or blocking.
    }
};
```

## Real-Time Rules

Inside `process()` and sample loops:

- Do not allocate or free memory.
- Do not perform file, console, device-enumeration, or other blocking I/O.
- Do not lock non-real-time mutexes.
- Do not throw exceptions.
- Do not resize beyond compile-time capacity.
- Validate configuration before processing starts.
- Use bounded SeRTial containers, fixed arrays, atomics, and deterministic loops.
- Preserve or deliberately update timestamps, sequence numbers, channel metadata, and flags.

`sertial::fixed_vector::push_back()` throws when full. Prove capacity before entering a real-time loop rather than relying on that exception.

Keep DSP code platform-independent. Treat standard-Linux tests as necessary but insufficient for changes to module execution, messaging, lifecycle, or backend code: those changes must also cross-compile against the RaTOS SDK and run under the EVL kernel in QEMU. Only physical-target measurements support latency, jitter, or dropout-resistance claims.

## Timing and Backend Boundaries

- Use `corerat::Time`, `corerat::Duration`, and `corerat::Thread` (or CommRaT aliases) for portable runtime timing and producer probes, not `std::chrono` or `std::this_thread` in EVL-capable producer paths.
- EVL waits require an EVL-attached thread. Construct probes on a platform-managed thread and fail explicitly if attachment failed; replacing the clock alone does not validate the EVL execution path.
- Schedule periodic producers with absolute platform-clock deadlines. Bounded pre-roll absorbs scheduling jitter but does not synchronize independent producer and hardware clocks; never describe it as a sustained drift fix.
- Ordinary ALSA calls are in-band. Keep the ALSA device worker on a standard thread; do not change it to an OOB thread merely to make its sleep use the platform abstraction. PipeWire owns its callback thread.
- Respect negotiated PCM buffer/period sizes and callback frame requests rather than assuming `period_frames` was accepted. Do not change system-wide PipeWire quantum settings to make a test pass.

## Parameters and Commands

Use typed parameters for persistent state that appears in configurations, presets, and RatGUI. Parameter structs must be reflectable aggregates with bounded field types.

Every configurable launchable module must publish `musicrat_parameters` metadata for its flat startup fields. Keep stable numeric parameter IDs with the owning protocol, use `text` for bounded string-backed values such as paths, and do not flatten nested aggregates such as `BeatGrid` until a structured editor contract exists. Only mark a parameter automatable when the module actually consumes it through a real-time parameter-event path.

Use output-associated commands only for imperative operations such as reset or loading a prepared resource. A command must define a `Reply` type and be registered with `register_command_handler`.

Do not introduce one command type per continuously changing knob when a timestamped control-event stream is appropriate.

## Launcher and Routing

Every independently launchable module must:

1. Have a small source file using `COMMRAT_MODULE_MAIN(ModuleType)`.
2. Be declared with `commrat_module()` in CMake.
3. Generate a complete `*.module.json` descriptor during native builds.
4. Have at least one example application config when it participates in a user-facing graph.
5. Publish `musicrat_ports` metadata for every physical output, input, synchronized input, and remote using stable IDs, exact positional indices, and the correct signal domain.

Use CommRaT application descriptions directly:

- `outputs` assigns output addresses in descriptor order.
- `inputs` routes continuous primary data.
- `synced_inputs` routes timestamp-correlated secondary data.
- `remotes` configures command/lifecycle targets.
- `params` supplies typed startup parameters.
- `companions` starts tools such as RatGUI.

Do not create a separate MusicRaT graph format. The Application Designer reads installed descriptors and edits the pre-launch CommRaT application description directly. RatGUI consumes the launched application description for runtime operation rather than owning pre-launch graph authoring.

## External Control

Hardware backends terminate in adapter modules. DSP modules consume semantic note, control, gate, trigger, or transport events and never parse MIDI, HID, OSC, or GPIO protocols directly.

High-rate controls are typed streaming inputs. Request/reply device operations are commands. Persistent source-to-parameter mappings belong to the graph/session model and include transforms, takeover behavior, and feedback routing.

## Build and Validation

Configure and build the current implementation with:

```bash
cmake -S . -B build-validation \
  -DBUILD_MUSICRAT=ON \
  -DBUILD_MUSICXML=OFF \
  -DBUILD_TESTING=ON
cmake --build build-validation -j2
ctest --test-dir build-validation --output-on-failure
```

Smoke-test the launcher with:

```bash
./build-validation/musicrat_launcher \
  ./examples/configs/sine_oscillator.json \
  --duration-ms 300
```

Tests should cover DSP kernels independently, message serialization, module behavior, descriptor generation, launcher routing, and real-time constraints. Keep tests deterministic and avoid requiring physical hardware unless explicitly marked as integration tests.

## Learnings

- Use CoreRaT's `corerat-router-tcp` on standard Linux and `corerat-router-evl` on RaTOS (the `corerat-router-evl.service` service), not the legacy `tims_router_tcp`. Check existing services before starting a router and never terminate another user's process.
- Build against a matching CommRaT package, headers, and descriptor-inspection macros. A local include override with stale installed macros can make descriptor generation fail even when the runtime compiles.
- Release SDKs must contain the pinned dependency headers and target development libraries, including ALSA. Private overlays are development diagnostics, not proof that the pinned SDK or image is reproducible.
- Keep physical testing separate from deployment: do not overwrite installed binaries or interrupt a running H4 graph without approval. Record exact revisions, backend, PCM geometry, duration, counters, and whether artifacts were dirty/development builds; absence of startup errors alone is not proof of clean audio.
- Follow the release pinning checklist in `docs/EVL_AND_RATOS.md`: clean upstream-matching worktrees, published dependency commits, exact recipe pins, regenerated SDK, then image build and installed-example validation after reboot.
